arxiv-1803-05284.title: A Unified View of False Discovery Rate Control: Reconciliation of Bayesian and Frequentist Approaches
arxiv-1803-05284.creator: Xiaoquan Wen
arxiv-1803-05284.description: Abstract This paper explores the intrinsic connections between the Bayesian false discovery rate (FDR) control procedures and their counterpart of frequentist procedures. We attempt to offer a unified view of FDR control within and beyond the setting of testing exchangeable hypotheses.

arxiv-2011-04760.title: Diamond Message Set Groupcasting: From an Inner Bound for the DM Broadcast Channel to the Capacity Region of the Combination Network Thanks: This work was presented in part at the 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Information Theory, LA, CA [ 1 ] . This research was funded in part by the 2018 and
arxiv-2011-04760.creator: Mohamed Salman, Mahesh K. Varanasi
arxiv-2011-04760.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Mohamed Salman, Mahesh K. Varanasi. Multiple groupcasting over the broadcast channel (BC) is studied in a special setting. In particular, an inner bound is obtained for the K K -receiver discrete memoryless (DM) BC for the diamond message set which consists of four groupcast messages: one desired by all receivers, one by all but two receivers, and two more desired by all but each one of those two receivers.

arxiv-2103-15348.title: LayoutParser : A Unified Toolkit for Deep Learning Based Document Image Analysis
arxiv-2103-15348.creator: Zejiang Shen (✉), Ruochen Zhang, Melissa Dell, Benjamin Charles Germain Lee, Jacob Carlson, Weining Li
arxiv-2103-15348.description: Abstract Recent advances in document image analysis (DIA) have been primarily driven by the application of neural networks. Ideally, research outcomes could be easily deployed in production and extended for further investigation. However, various factors like loosely organized codebases and sophisticated model configurations complicate the easy reuse of important innovations by a wide audience.

arxiv-2109-02870.title: Convergence of a spectral regularization of a time-reversed reaction-diffusion problem with high-order Sobolev-Gevrey smoothness
arxiv-2109-02870.creator: Vo Anh Khoa
arxiv-2109-02870.description: Abstract . The present paper analyzes a spectral regularization of a time-reversed reaction-diffusion problem with globally and locally Lipschitz nonlinearities. This type of inverse and ill-posed problems arises in a variety of real-world applications concerning heat conduction and tumour source localization.

arxiv-2203-03447.title: A solar-cycle study of coronal rotation: large variations, rapid changes, and implications for solar wind models
arxiv-2203-03447.creator: Liam Edwards, David Kuridze, Thomas Williams, Huw Morgan
arxiv-2203-03447.description: Abstract Information on the rotation rate of the corona, and its variation over latitude and solar cycle, is valuable for making global connections between the corona and the Sun, for global estimates of reconnection rates, and as a basic parameter for solar wind modelling.

arxiv-2412-05449.title: Towards Effective GenAI Multi-Agent Collaboration: Design and Evaluation for Enterprise Applications
arxiv-2412-05449.creator: Raphael Shu, Nilaksh Das, Michelle Yuan, Monica Sunkara, Yi Zhang
arxiv-2412-05449.description: Abstract AI agents powered by large language models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities in problem solving. Through combining many intelligent agents, multi-agent collaboration has emerged as a promising approach to tackle complex, multi-faceted problems that exceed the capabilities of single AI agents.

arxiv-2512-13708.title: Variational Physics-Informed Ansatz for Reconstructing Hidden Interaction Networks from Steady States
arxiv-2512-13708.creator: Kaiming Luo
arxiv-2512-13708.description: Abstract The interaction structure of a complex dynamical system governs its collective behavior, yet existing reconstruction methods struggle with nonlinear, heterogeneous, and higher-order couplings—especially when only steady states are observable. We propose a Variational Physics-Informed Ansatz (VPIA) that infers general interaction operators directly from heterogeneous steady-state data.

arxiv-2512-16426.title: Calculation of hyperfine structure in Tm ii
arxiv-2512-16426.creator: Andrey I. Bondarev
arxiv-2512-16426.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Andrey I. Bondarev. The first measurements of the magnetic dipole hyperfine structure constants A A in singly ionized thulium revealed substantial discrepancies with the corresponding calculations [Mansour et al., NIMB 40, 252 (1989)]. More recent measurements [Kebapcı et al., ApJ 970, 23 (2024)] expanded very limited dataset of that work and demonstrated that two of the previously reported experimental A A values were incorrect, motivating new theoretical calculations.

pmc-10672123.title: Intraoral Microvascular Anastomosis in Immediate Free Flap Reconstruction for Midfacial Tumor Defects: A Retrospective Multicenter Study
pmc-10672123.creator: Peer W. Kämmerer, Milad Tavakoli, Alexander Gaggl, Massimo Maranzano
pmc-10672123.description: (1) Background: The current landscape of midface reconstruction is marked by ongoing evolution, with notable advancements in surgical techniques, microvascular procedures, and the implementation of multidisciplinary approaches, all of which have significantly enhanced both functional and aesthetic outcomes. Conventionally, microvascular anastomoses for free flaps in midfacial reconstruction have been executed using cervical vessels.

pmc-10711479.title: Missense variants in SORT1 are associated with LDL-C in an Amish population
pmc-10711479.creator: Kelly A. Mitok, Kathryn L. Schueler, Sarah M. King, Joseph Orr, Kathleen A. Ryan, Mark P. Keller, Ronald M. Krauss, Braxton D. Mitchell, Alan R. Shuldiner, Alan D. Attie
pmc-10711479.description: Common noncoding variants at the human 1p13.3 locus associated with SORT1 expression are among those most strongly associated with low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in human genome-wide association studies. However, validation studies in mice and cell lines have produced variable results regarding the directionality of the effect of SORT1 on LDL-C. This, together with the fact that the 1p13.

pmc-11447191.title: The relevance of tumor target expression levels on IgA-mediated cytotoxicity in cancer immunotherapy
pmc-11447191.creator: Chilam Chan, Núria Casalé Cabanes, J. H. Marco Jansen, Joël Guillaume, Maaike Nederend, Elsemieke M. Passchier, Valentina E. Gómez-Mellado, Matthias Peipp, Marianne Boes, Geert van Tetering, Jeanette H. W. Leusen
pmc-11447191.description: Recent advances in cancer immunotherapy, particularly the success of immune checkpoint inhibitors, have reignited interest in targeted monoclonal antibodies for immunotherapy. Antibody therapies aim to minimize on-target, off-tumor toxicity by targeting antigens overexpressed on tumor cells but not on healthy cells. Despite considerable efforts, some therapeutic antibodies have been linked to dose-limiting side effects.

pmc-11562580.title: Do You Want to Make a Battery? Insights from the Development and Evaluation of a Chemistry Public Engagement Activity
pmc-11562580.creator: John O’Donoghue, Natalia García Doménech, Dearbhla Tully, Niamh McGoldrick, Fiona McArdle, Mary Connolly, David J Otway, Will Daly, Lynette Keeney, Mervyn Horgan
pmc-11562580.description: Chemistry is often associated with formal learning environments and has been described as overly serious by the general public, lacking some of the fun and energy of other sciences. However, it is difficult to provide hands-on chemistry activities outside the lab and other formal learning environments.

pmc-11692241.title: HISTORY OF HEALTH INSURANCE COVERAGE GAPS AND HEALTH CARE USE AFTER GAINING AGE-BASED MEDICARE COVERAGE
pmc-11692241.creator: Jada Morris, Dmitry Tumin, Yan Zhang
pmc-11692241.description: This study investigates the relationship between gaps in health insurance coverage prior to Medicare eligibility and subsequent changes in healthcare utilization among older adults in the United States. Medicare serves as the primary healthcare system for individuals aged 65 and above, offering access to essential medical services and security to seniors nationwide.

pmc-11738112.title: Depression and the Risk Factors Among Elderly Residents in Gyeongsangbuk-Do
pmc-11738112.creator: M.D. Kwang Hun Lee
pmc-11738112.description: AimsThe purpose of this study is to analyze the prevalence and factors of depression among the elderly population, a significant issue in Korea's aging society. By doing so, we aim to provide basic indicators for improving mental health and quality of life while efficiently managing healthcare costs.

pmc-12932274.title: Repeat resection for recurrent glioblastoma – does timing matter?
pmc-12932274.creator: Obada T Alhalabi, Kirill Mironov, Khurshed Nabiev, Johanna Krämer, Nour Gareib, Henri Olldashi, Stefan Joser, Marianne Schell, Sandro M Krieg, Andreas W Unterberg, Christine Jungk
pmc-12932274.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe optimal timing of repeat surgical resection in patients with recurrent IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (rGB) remains unclear. We aimed to characterize temporal patterns between radiological suspicion of recurrence and repeat resection and to evaluate the impact of early versus delayed surgery on the extent of resection (EOR), functional outcomes, adjuvant therapy, and survivalMethodsWe retrospectively analyzed a consecutive cohort of 150 patients who underwent resection for histopathologically confirmed rGB between 2015 and 2023 at a single tertiary care center.

pmc-12973831.title: Prognostic impact of myelodysplasia-related gene mutations in ELN-2022 favorable-risk acute myeloid leukemia subtypes
pmc-12973831.creator: Lulu Zhang, Shuangwei Ying, Fang Fang, Qian Li, Furun An, Jingwen Li, Jie Sun, Weiyan Zheng, Zhimin Zhai, Yuanyuan Zhu
pmc-12973831.description: ABSRACTBackgroundThe 2022 European Leukemia Net (ELN) risk stratification categorizes acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with myelodysplasia-related gene (MRG) mutations - including ASXL1, BCOR, EZH2, RUNX1, SF3B1, SRSF2, STAG2, U2AF1 and/or ZRSR2 - as “adverse-risk”. However, the prognostic relevance of MRG mutations in patients with favorable-risk AML remains uncertain.

pmc-13055837.title: Cross‐Platform Proteomics and Machine Learning Algorithms Nominate Plasma Biomarkers of Stroke Diagnosis
pmc-13055837.creator: Shubham Misra, Wooyoung Eric Jang, Sebastian Sanchez, Aditya Natu, Prateek Kumar, Michael Liu, Anmol Kaur, Victor Torres Lopez, Pinar Caglayan, Rolando Garcia‐Milian, Caroline M. Watson, Michael R. Frankel, Guido J. Falcone, Lauren H. Sansing, Srikant Rangaraju
pmc-13055837.description: BackgroundBlood‐based biomarkers for stroke subtyping could improve triage in emergency settings. We used cross‐platform proteomics to identify plasma biomarkers differentiating major stroke diagnostic groups.MethodsWe conducted a case–control study using 2 biorepositories. Plasma was collected in the emergency department from adults with suspected stroke before therapeutic intervention.

pmc-13188344.title: Application of contrast-enhanced CT-based radiomics with machine learning to predict WHO/ISUP grading in clear cell renal cell carcinoma
pmc-13188344.creator: Xiaowei Li, Shiyan Song, Wenfei Ge, Haicheng Wang, Wei Liu, Xiaochen Qi, Yuming Zhao
pmc-13188344.description: ObjectiveTo predict the World Health Organization (WHO)/International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) grading of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) using multiple machine learning models based on contrast-enhanced CT, and to compare their performance, thereby exploring a non-invasive method for preoperative pathological grading.MethodsSeventy-six patients with ccRCC (65 low-grade and 11 high-grade) from September 2021 to August 2023 were retrospectively included.

pmc-13466857.title: Inflammatory Biomarkers and Delirium Severity in Critically Ill Adults: A Prospective Single-Center Cohort Study
pmc-13466857.creator: Mateusz Szczupak, Marek Konop, Sabina Krupa-Nurcek
pmc-13466857.description: Background: This study examined associations between C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), ordinal procalcitonin (PCT) categories, and delirium severity in critically ill adults. Secondary exploratory analyses evaluated whether baseline CRP and IL-6 discriminated subsequent incident delirium and remained associated with this outcome after adjustment. Methods: This prospective observational cohort included 267 adults treated in a general intensive care unit.
